about_this_copy: NASA TN D-6425 figure 7, the rudder-0 curves only (circles and their repeat squares), read for FSG milestone 3, pull request 10 (round 3), so that the F-4C file can take the report's bend of yaw, roll and side force with large sideslip. The values are the report's own coefficients, as printed (body axes, about 33% of the mean chord, the report's wing area and span); tools/f4c-sideslip.mjs moves them to AFWAL's reference and works out the file's tables.

source.title: Static Force Tests of a Model of a Twin-Jet Fighter Airplane for Angles of Attack from -10 to 110 deg and Sideslip Angles from -40 to 40 deg
source.author: Ernie L. Anglin, Langley Research Center
source.figure: Figure 7, Effect of rudder deflection on the static lateral-directional stability coefficients as a function of angle of attack and sideslip angle, delta_h = 0 (panels a to z, -10 to 110 degrees)
source.model: 0.13-scale model of the F-4 ("twin-jet high-performance fighter airplane designed for land and carrier-based operations"), clean, horizontal tail at 0, Langley full-scale tunnel (30 by 60 ft open throat); "the present tests were conducted at a tunnel velocity approximately equal to the expected velocity of the proposed free-flight model during spins" (low speed; Reynolds number not stated in the text read)

axes_and_reference.axes: body axes (the report's symbols section and its figure 1: "All forces and moments presented herein are referred to the body system of axes")
axes_and_reference.moment_reference: 33 percent of the mean aerodynamic chord
axes_and_reference.to_afwal: AFWAL's model is body-axis moments about 31% of the chord with 530 sq ft and a 38.67 ft span. The side force is multiplied by S_report/S_afwal (1.0157); the rolling moment by S b over S b (1.0089); the yawing moment is first moved 0.02 chord (0.321 ft) forward, Cn31 = Cn33 - (0.321/38.41) Cy, then multiplied by 1.0089. Each change is under 5% of a slope; tools/f4c-sideslip.mjs applies all three.

how_read.images: The PDF's own scans (pdfimages: 1-bit CCITT at 300 dpi), not re-rendered. Page 38 is turned 1.05 degrees in the scan and was turned back first; the other pages lean under 0.2 degrees, left as they are (under 3 px across a plot).
how_read.calibration: Sideslip: the plotted sideslip lines found in the scan (columns with long dark runs), each snapped to its expected place and fitted with a straight line (residual under 4 px). Coefficients: the printed axis labels found as rows of digits left of the plot frame, fitted with a straight line (residual under 3 px); where the label finder failed (alpha 25 rolling moment; 50; 60; 80, 85 and 100 yawing moment; 110) the label rows were read from 2x views and are named "manual" below.
how_read.reading_A: Automatic: at each sideslip line a search for the rudder-0 symbol (a ring: circle or square, scored on all four quadrants so that the triangles of the other two rudder settings score lower), the one nearest reading B within 0.008 (yaw, roll) or 0.06 (side force) taken, its centre converted by the calibration. At alpha 50 (symbols filled) and 110 (labels touching the frame) reading A is a magnified eye reading (2.5 to 3 times the views of reading B).
how_read.reading_B: By eye, done first and without reading A: every rudder-0 symbol read on views of the whole page at 0.36 to 0.5 scale. From -10 to 22.5 degrees reading B was taken as pixel positions and converted with reading A's calibration, so the two share their calibration there; from 25 degrees up reading B was read against the printed labels, independently.
how_read.reading_error: Taken as the root-mean-square difference of the two readings: about 0.0025 in yawing moment, 0.002 in rolling moment and 0.014 in side force (reading B is the coarser of the two). Where they differ by more than 0.005 (yaw, roll) or 0.03 (side force) the measured reading A is used; at 80 degrees, where reading B differed by up to 0.008 in yawing moment, a 2x view of the plot confirmed reading A (reading B had misread that page's scale).
how_read.flags: "measured": reading A, automatic; "magnified eye reading": reading A by eye on a 2.5 to 3x view; "eyeballed": reading B only, where reading A found no symbol. Nothing is interpolated between points: a point the plot does not show is left out.

page_40_scale: Panels (i) and (j), 20 and 22.5 degrees, are drawn about 1.6 times larger than the others, and their yawing-moment axis is printed .4, .2, 0, -.2, -.4. Read as .04, .02, 0, -.02, -.04: on that reading the rudder's effect at zero sideslip (about 0.015) and the slope at small sideslip (+0.0008 per degree at 20, -0.0015 at 22.5) sit between those of the panels either side (17.5: +0.0013; 25: -0.0011); on the printed scale both would be ten times larger. The side force (.2 a label, as printed) and rolling moment (.02) on that page are read as printed. Reasoned from that continuity; the two panels are used.
side_force_above_70_degrees: AFWAL's CYB is positive from 70 degrees up (+0.0006 at 70, +0.003 at 80 to 110: afwal-f4j.json as the listing prints it). The report agrees within 10 degrees of sideslip: its small-sideslip slope is positive or near zero there too (+0.0018 at 70, +0.0016 at 75, -0.0005 and +0.0002 at 80 and 85, +0.0011 to +0.0026 at 90 to 110; the cross-check below), never the large negative slope of its overall trend, while past about 15 degrees its side force falls steeply (about -0.003 a degree overall from -40 to 40). So the record matches the print and both are right: the positive slope is the small-sideslip part only, and the bend beyond 10 degrees (this record) carries the rest. Listed as a doubt resolved, nothing changed.

cross_check_within_10_degrees.how: The report's slope over plus and minus 10 degrees (the odd part, (C(beta) - C(-beta))/2, at 5 and 10 degrees, least squares through zero), moved to AFWAL's reference, beside AFWAL's per-degree table at the same angle of attack (its value at |alpha| for a negative angle, as AFWAL's Table 1 does; CNB1 held at 45 above 45).
cross_check_within_10_degrees.finding: Below the stall AFWAL's slopes are not this report's: yawing moment 18 to 21% larger in the report from -10 to 5 degrees, side force 14 to 22% larger, and the rolling moment at 0 degrees 41% smaller, and the rolling moment at negative angles of attack of the other sign (at -10 degrees +0.0005 against AFWAL's -0.0024). AFWAL says why: its model below about 30 degrees is its reference 16 (STI's F-4J data package, from McDonnell's spin-evaluation data, NASA Langley tabulations and NASA's simulator data, normalised to trim Mach number), and this report gave only the trends beyond (AFWAL-TR-80-3141 Part III, section E, PDF p.38-39). Through the stall and above, the two differ by more again. That is why only the report's departure from its own straight line is used beyond 10 degrees, never its level.
